- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e030d436bf0a3244502e021fe53035fc6b7b28da` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin 08ebfd94f93c96c37ae63cbdc985ee10fe572931 && git checkout 08ebfd94f93c96c37ae63cbdc985ee10fe572931
```

- **The notes, and what this PR changes under them.** Both are unreleased; the Version Packages PR #21988 is still open.
  - `.changeset/22256-migrate-meta-load-path-conversions.md` (PR #22351) loses one bullet: "Known limit, unchanged. Inside a `composeStacks([…])` project … a conversion the load still applies inside a package body is still not listed, and `--write` still does not write it."

  - This PR removes that limit, so restoring the old text would publish a false release note in the same `@objectstack/cli` release.
- **The confirmation:** the seat review `6072731732` on #22256 accepts the correction under `os-dev.md`. It was declared to the owning `domain:cli` seat on #6024 in this act. That seat or the maintainer may overrule it on this PR before it lands.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, with my verdict on it.

1. **`@objectstack/spec` · `defineStack(config, options)` honours one undeclared symbol key** — `Symbol.for('objectstack.stack.authoredInput')` (`AUTHORED_INPUT_OPTION`, `stack.zod.ts`), read only when `strict: false`; its whole effect is `convert: strict || !asksForAuthoredInput(options)` on the `normalizeStackInput` call, so the ADR-0087 D2 pass is skipped while map-to-array normalisation, the bound-action merge and the provenance mark still happen. By the repo's own definition of the published accept-set (reachable from the entry type graph and addressable through `exports`): `DefineStackOptions` is unchanged, nothing new is exported from `src/index.ts` (the only spellings in the tree are the constant in `stack.zod.ts`, prose in `stack-provenance.ts`, and the CLI's own `SPEC_AUTHORED_INPUT_OPTION`), and `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` are green inside `TypeScript Type Check` with no regenerated artefact. A TypeScript caller reaches it only through a cast. **Right: off the public entry; `Clause-②: no` stands.** Four things checked in the diff rather than taken from the report: (a) the strict arm is unreachable — `strict ||` short-circuits, so a strict call converts regardless of the key (pinned in `stack-authored-input.test.ts`); (b) it adds no capability a public caller lacks — `normalizeStackInput(…, { convert: false })` is exported from `index.ts` and `NormalizeStackInputOptions.convert` documents exactly this consumer; (c) a non-strict output is already judged by nothing, so an unconverted non-strict stack sits in the trust class non-strict output already had; (d) the `Symbol.for` crossing is the provenance mark's own precedent in `stack-provenance.ts`, and the CLI's `AUTHORED_ARGUMENT_KEY` from the one-package half uses it too.
2. **The provenance mark's meaning gains one exception**: a marked stack may carry an unconverted spelling when, and only when, it was produced through item 1. Declared at both sites (the `stack-provenance.ts` module header, the `AUTHORED_INPUT_OPTION` docblock), and the doors that report conversions already re-run their own pass over what they load. **Right** — a declared producer mode, not a consumer accommodation; Prime Directive #12 is not touched.
3. **`composeStacks` accept-set: unchanged.** An input produced through item 1 carries the mark, so it passes the `STACK_PROVENANCE_MISSING` gate exactly as any non-strict output does; a plain object or a spread still fails it, because the shim's `__composable` hands every input it did not see a `defineStack` call build through untouched. Body assembly stays composition's rule in `packages/spec`; the CLI prelude only re-produces inputs and calls the real `composeStacks`. **Right**, and the `domain:cli` seat's cut (no second copy of composition's rule) holds in the diff.
4. **`@objectstack/cli` · `os migrate meta` on a `composeStacks([…], { manifest: 'preserve' })` project** now lists a load-path conversion under its body path (`packages[i].manifest…`) and `--write` writes it into the file that authored input i. The key is passed by the authored-source load (`loadConfig({ authoredSource: true })`) alone, and the strict load every other command uses is pinned to keep converting (`'mongodb'` in its body). A canonical composed project is pinned to write nothing and to give the summary the built composition gives. **Right** — this is the card's stage-2 accept-set as triage routed it (card comment 6070653436, with the dev's H4 case as the pin); it widens what the command lists, not what it accepts.
5. **The `--out` snapshot of a composed project** drops the keys the schema's parse fills in from each package body (the dev's reading on `app-multi-package`: 53 keys present only on BASE, none added, no value changed). **Right** — the shape ruling A (REWORK 6068295985) already accepted for one-package stacks, extended to the bodies; the new changeset states it.
6. **Single-input `composeStacks([x])`** (PR acceptance note 2): because `composeStacks` returns a single input untouched and the re-produced `x` no longer carries the CLI's `AUTHORED_ARGUMENT_KEY`, the chain now receives `x` normalised with its bound actions merged instead of the raw literal. `applied` and `--write` are unaffected (`meta.ts` normalises before the chain either way); only `--out` can differ, and only with bound standalone actions. **Right as declared**, with one note for the `domain:cli` carrier: on that edge the single-input snapshot now differs from the one-package snapshot (actions merged vs not), which ruling A's one-snapshot-shape intent did not foresee. It is an acceptance note, not in the changeset. No accept-set or key moves; not blocking.
7. **`SPEC_AUTHORED_INPUT_OPTION` duplicates the registry name in `packages/cli`.** Drift is not silent — the producer then converts as before and the composed pins go red on the very conversion — and the docblock says so. **Right.**
8. **`meta.ts`**: comment only, verified in the diff. **Right.**

Not implied by the diff: no REST route, no schema key, no retired key, no ADR-governed decision reversed (`docs/adr/**` untouched; the ADR-0087 id is left in the code at the seam).
